Author says buffer and prepared code unchanged, gains come from underlying structures. Absolute timings are unitless; 2021-era blog, dataset not given here. NEWS.md (libgeos/geos main) also lists later perf items with no numbers: 3.10 TemplateSTRtree, 3.12 prepared polygon intersection GH-690, distance GH-693, coverage union GH-681, 3.13 distance/convex hull, 3.14 RelateNG prepared A/L GH-1201, 3.15 overlay GH-1353. Only one numeric claim on NEWS: 3.2.0 buffer q:"20x for a case in testsuite". single-source for the table. Overlap: none known

Polygon geometry is identical after normalization but raw WKT differs, so the gate needs normalization. LGPL licence needs a reviewer decision. Details in /work/SPIKE.md.

spike_plan.kill_if: 3.9 diverges from 3.8 WKT on a broad class of inputs (then K5 or K4: the reference cannot pass the identical-output gate) OR the speedup is under 1.2x on overlay and union.
spike_plan.pass_if: 3.9 WKT matches 3.8 on 99.9% or more of cases (or a pre-agreed tolerance) AND 3.9 is at least 1.5x faster than 3.8 on at least two operations.
steps: In a throwaway networked Linux container, clone libgeos/geos at tags 3.8.0 and 3.9.0 and build both with CMake (Release, same flags).
Write a driver that generates random point/circle sets (STRtree envelope and NN) and watershed-like polygon sets (union, intersection, difference) with fixed seeds.
Run both builds on the same inputs; diff WKT outputs over at least 10k cases including near-degenerate polygons.
Measure medians of 5 runs per operation for 3.8 and 3.9; record the speedup per operation.
Run the GEOS unit tests on 3.9 and count the test cases.
Repeat the timing run 3 times to check determinism.

v1.summary: GEOS 3.8.0 to 3.9.0 is a real, public, pinned pair with a confirmed tag and changelog, and the blog's 86/85/36 percent figures are confirmed as single-source numbers from one dataset, with no overlay headline figure. The main open risk is that the 3.9 reference replaced the overlay engine with OverlayNG and may not reproduce 3.8 WKT, so the spike must first test whether the reference passes the identical-output gate; the LGPL-2.1 licence needs a reviewer decision.

v2.note: Real release pair: 3.8.0 to 3.9.0 is confirmed, and the 86% / 85% / 36% blog gains are confirmed but come from one post. Several separate levers: STRtree query, nearest neighbour, unary union, overlay. Main flaw: OverlayNG changes vertex order and noding, so a gate requiring identical WKT against 3.8 would likely fail the reference itself. The gate must be normalized or topological equality, computed by a sealed GEOS. STRtree results must be compared as sets. LGPL-2.1 allows shipping with source (Lic 4). Speedups must be re-measured on the hidden datasets under gVisor, since the blog numbers are for one machine. Porting OverlayNG without JTS offline is large, so the expected trial path is STRtree gains plus partial union and overlay gains.
